blocks.text: Imports React hooks, event clients, API helpers, and UI utilities. The provider begins by declaring context state for the active session and the live execution surfaces.
blocks.title: Context dependencies and initial state

blocks.text: This section tracks agent steps, routing traces, approvals, batches, progress, and related server-backed state. It establishes the state that later event handlers and callbacks update.
blocks.title: Live execution and approval state

blocks.text: Effects subscribe to Pusher agent events and the ticket-authenticated WebSocket used for upload/topic updates. Cleanup removes listeners, closes connections, and revokes resources where applicable.
blocks.title: Realtime subscriptions

blocks.text: Callbacks load session details and coordinate agent runs, steps, approvals, routing, batches, and progress. They translate API responses into provider state and expose actions to consumers.
blocks.title: Session and agent operations

blocks.text: Workspace, file, upload, and ingestion callbacks call the backend and refresh or update the corresponding state. These operations cover local artifacts as well as streamed processing progress.
blocks.title: Workspace and ingestion operations

blocks.text: Notebook helpers and hardware-related callbacks manage notebook resources, device specifications, cluster/candidate review, and related loading or error state.
blocks.title: Notebook, device, and review APIs

blocks.text: The provider creates template runs, tracks media object URLs, and dispatches tasks. Side effects are kept behind memoized callbacks so consumers receive stable operations.
blocks.title: Templates, media, and task dispatch

blocks.text: The final section assembles all state values and callbacks into the memoized context value. SessionProvider renders the provider around children and exposes the complete shared session API.
blocks.title: Public context surface

gotchas: This provider is intentionally broad: its value spans live execution, file operations, ingestion, notebooks, hardware review, media, and templates.
The exact event payloads and endpoint behavior are defined by the callbacks and server APIs used throughout the provider.
Object URLs require cleanup when media state changes or the provider unmounts.
how_it_works: Initializes session, agent, routing, approval, batch, workspace, notebook, device, and review state
Loads and mutates server-backed session resources through callbacks
Subscribes to live agent and upload/topic events and maintains object URLs
Exports one memoized context object through SessionContext.Provider
outputs: React context value containing state and operations
purpose: SessionProvider centralizes the active session and its related UI data. It subscribes to Pusher and ticket-authenticated WebSocket events, exposes callbacks for agent work, approvals, files, notebooks, ingestion, devices, clusters, templates, and task dispatch, then memoizes the context value.
summary: Provides the shared React session state, live events, approvals, workspace APIs, and task operations to the frontend.

symbols.summary: Provides shared session state and server/realtime operations to descendant React components.
